niche_preference_profile: Prefers calm, polished consumer-app interfaces that feel light, soft, and emotionally welcoming. They consistently favor clear hierarchy, fewer but larger content groupings, generous spacing, guided step-by-step flows, warm human or lifestyle imagery, restrained accent use, and supportive copy. They generally like screens that feel curated rather than fragmented, with strong section separation, smooth rounded shapes, and a composed visual rhythm over dense, promotional, or overly technical layouts.

criteria.description: Prefers strong, legible hierarchy with clearly separated sections, distinct grouping, and an obvious focal path rather than flat or fragmented layouts.
Prefers guided, step-by-step onboarding with paced progression cues such as carousels, steppers, or explicit next actions rather than checklist-like or static informational presentations.
Prefers warm photographic hero imagery and human or lifestyle context that adds emotional softness and approachability over abstract icons or colder technical visuals.
Prefers a softer, lighter, more breathable visual rhythm with airy spacing and reduced harshness rather than heavy, dense, or enterprise-like compositions.
Prefers fewer, larger, consolidated panels or cards that unify content instead of many repeated mini-cards, nested modules, or fragmented boxed items.
Prefers reassuring, calm, user-centered presentation and copy that feels supportive and understated rather than promotional, alarmist, or theatrically branded.
Prefers generously rounded cards, controls, and modal shapes that create a cushioned, contemporary feel over sharper or more rigid geometry.
Prefers explicit progression controls and progress feedback, such as anchored next/back actions, carousel dots, or footer steppers, that make movement through the flow feel decisive.
Prefers restrained, disciplined accent usage with calmer color application and fewer loud color pops rather than saturated, varied, or high-energy accent treatments.
Prefers concise, directly framed content with short supportive text and scannable grouping rather than verbose explanations, repeated labels, or feature-heavy copy blocks.
